thread:
Carla: Customer (Acme) reported intermittent failures from /v1/invoices generate -> schema validation errors. Says invoice.id sometimes arrives as "12345" (string) and status comes back as "PENDING" which fails enum casing.
Ben (support): Can you paste the raw model response they sent or a minimal repro? Any stack traces?
Carla: Here's the snippet customer pasted (they're on Dedicated):
```
{"invoice": {"id": "12345", "amount": 1999, "active": "false", "status": "PENDING"}}
```
They get parser errors in our strict JSON mode: "schema error: field 'invoice.id' expected number got string" and also "enum mismatch: 'PENDING' not in ["pending","issued","paid"]".
Alice (eng): Is this definitely model output as JSON, or could it be a streaming chunk boundary that left quotes in place? Any truncation logs? Also, any correlation with long generations/latency?
Carla: Customer says it happens more when the response is > ~1200 tokens and when they hit a latency spike. We found a runtime log with a connection reset around the same time:
```
[runtime] trace_id=tr_9f3a: connection reset by peer during stream write -> client saw partial chunk
[json-parse] unexpected token '"' at position 1
```
Ben (support): Ok. Can we repro locally? Carla, can you ask for a raw fetch with --raw-streaming header? Also provide the trace_id to eng.
Carla: Sent repro curl they ran:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: application/json+stream" \
  -d '{"prompt":"...long prompt...","json_mode":"strict"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer > response.ndjson
```
Result: sometimes lines look like:
```
{"invoice":{"id":"12345","amount":1999,"active":"false","status":"PENDING"}}

{"invoice":{"id":12345,"amount":1999,"active":false,"status":"pending"}}
```
Alice (eng): That alternating output pattern strongly suggests model stochasticity combined with stream reconstruction issues. If a chunk boundary splits tokens like true/false or quotes, clients parsing strict JSON will fail. Two immediate mitigations: 1) recommend customer disable strict json_mode or enable permissive/coerce mode (client side). 2) runtime: add a short buffer/reassembly window on stream boundary and detect truncated tokens before emitting chunk.
runtime-bot: Logged incident INC-2026; assigned to eng-runtime; added trace_id tr_9f3a and affected host host-12gpu-04.
Ben (support): I'll ask Acme if they can toggle to json_mode=permissive for now and share exact reproduction steps + response.ndjson. Also check if they're on a Dedicated with any proxy in front.
Carla: Customer confirmed they can test permissive mode and will send back the ndjson and the SDK call id. Opening a support ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/ACME-521
Alice (eng): Eng-runtime: please prioritize a short-term patch to reassemble partial tokens at stream boundaries. If not feasible, at least detect malformed JSON in stream and emit a parse-friendly fallback object with "_malformed":true and original_chunk base64 so clients can get a consistent envelope.
Ben (support): Noted. I'll keep customer updated. Marking as P1 due to billing pipeline downstream consumers failing validation.
Carla: Thanks — will forward any customer files as soon as they arrive. :thumbsup:
